beginner.headline: Today (Thu Oct 15): conditional for beginners. Best 6:45–9:30 AM around the 7:13 AM high (1.9 ft), before the trades strengthen. Canoes small now (1–2 ft knee–thigh), but a 19–20 s south swell is building: fewer, stronger sets, biggest later in the day. Afternoon not recommended for beginners.
beginner.recommendation: Go early: 6:45–9:30 AM gives the most water over the reef (7:13 AM high, 1.9 ft) and the lightest wind of the day (trades in the teens this morning; Surfline model 11 kt ENE gusting 20 now). Canoes is small this morning, but don't read that as low-energy: the new swell is 19–20 s and building, so lulls are long and the odd set has far more push than the average wave. Watch several full set cycles (10+ minutes) before starting and re-check every half hour as the swell fills. ENE trades are cross-offshore at Waikīkī, so expect seaward drift, worse on gusts and after mid-morning. The DOH list was not read: check water color at Canoes and toward the Kūhiō drains and Ala Wai side; brown, gray or cloudy water ends it. One student or a small group of strong adults; several students or children only if drift is low and sets aren't reaching the inside. Your on-site read overrides this report.
